name: Galióin

attributes.attribute: was an Irish mythological race of uncertain origin
joined the invading Fir Bolg and served Queen Medb
was persuaded to keep the Galióin by her lover Fergus mac Róich

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Galióin was an Irish mythological race. Sources also call the tribe Gailioin, Gálian, or Galioin. The settlers had an unclear heritage. They appear in the Book of Invasions and in the Táin Bó Cuailnge. In the Book of Invasions they joined the invading Fir Bolg. In the Táin their fierceness frightened Queen Medb. Fergus mac Róich spread them among the troops. They proved a useful asset. They may represent an early Celtic tribal group.

okr.objective: Record the Irish mythological race of the Galióin.
key_results: Name the alternate spellings Gailioin, Gálian, and Galioin.
Place the Galióin in the Book of Invasions and the Táin Bó Cuailnge.
Describe their service to Queen Medb under the counsel of Fergus mac Róich.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore, 2008, s.v. 'Galióin'.
